key_insight: In both spin-coated and gravure-printed PM6:Y12 organic solar cells, photodegradation is governed by the mobility-lifetime product μτ, making it a unified descriptor that connects microscopic ageing changes to efficiency loss.
engineering_relevance: For scalable OSC manufacturing, this shows that improving lifetime alone is not enough; device optimization must preserve charge-carrier mobility and morphology to sustain performance.
method: Compared spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 devices.
Tracked continuous illumination ageing for ~1000 h.
Linked changes in mobility, recombination lifetime, and morphology to power-conversion efficiency loss.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic PCE degradation across both device types during ~1000 h illumination, with printed devices showing increased lifetime but strongly reduced mobility, and the performance loss following μτ.
watch_item: The printed architecture shows a metastable dark-recovery contribution, so degradation behavior may depend on measurement history and processing route, not just steady-state lifetime.
paper_title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
